ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The Way does not belong to knowing is Nanquan Puyuan’s case formula, completed by the equal refusal that it belongs to not-knowing.
EvidenceBody: When Zhaozhou asks how one can know the Way without aiming toward it, Nanquan says the Way belongs neither to knowing nor not-knowing: knowing is delusive awareness and not-knowing is blank indeterminacy. Later records repeatedly raise the complete exchange.

Tianran Hanshi calls it Zhaozhou’s obtaining the substance. A later questioner invokes the line beside “Chan is not conceptual imagining” and demands a response outside both routes, showing that the proposition remains live interview material.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A proposition about knowing becomes the hinge of a public exchange: Nanquan cuts off both knowledge and blank unknowing, and later questioners use his words to demand a fresh answer.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The second half is indispensable. Translating only an attack on knowledge would conceal Nanquan’s simultaneous rejection of not-knowing.

ComparedThings: later raisings and tests of that proposition
DifferentThingTest.Reason: Later speakers explicitly cite and test the same formula.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The aliases include the full two-sided Nanquan formula.
